prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: []
1: ["Next, verify how your pet looks on your desktop screen."]
2: ["Master Your Desktop Pet Controls", "Learn quick shortcuts to interact with, move, or hide your companion anytime.", "Desktop Gestures & Controls"]
3: ["Preparing Desktop Pet Assets", "We are generating your desktop pet animations. Relax or set a system alert!", "Tip: You can drag your pet across multi-monitor setups anytime."]
4: ["Sign In to Sync & Restore Your Pets", "Sign in with your existing account to prevent pet resets and keep your desktop companions safe."]
5: ["For best results, upload clear, well-lit photos with a single centered subject."]
6: ["Feel free to minimize this window. We will notify you when your pet is ready!"]
7: ["Select Your Adoption Journey", "Choose standard adoption or create a custom pet companion."]
8: ["Select a path to unlock unique desktop behaviors for your pet!"]
9: ["Your pet is now live! Access quick controls anytime from your system taskbar tray."]
